The core gimmick of this build is to combine [Frost Armor](item_f9925f6e-bb6a-4de6-bb86-622583d60779) with [Martian Mender](item_0099632b-4e18-450e-844f-22c40e51bc98) for an efficiently-priced pool of self-regenerating Armor. However, since that gimmick is out of reach until *at least* Round 2, it's better to start off with pure damage so you can farm more $ and hopefully secure a few eliminations.

To that end, [Extendothermics](item_501fc89f-a7b4-46c5-a43f-b65ab0958438) will give you an early edge. You're still gonna want to launch icicles until a brawl breaks out, but once you've properly engaged the enemy, having a +60% range boost to your ultra-reliable primary fire is huge. Whether you're chasing or kiting, this power helps you to maintain optimal positioning.

As for starting items, [Ammo Reserves](item_982d53aa-5ef4-493f-93e7-9e374d0ebf34), [Weapon Grease](item_961ae72f-434f-406b-a89b-ab8efec806bf), and [Compensator](item_2a354f80-610c-4661-9bdd-8960ae1a60b0) are the way to go. If you're winning, win harder. If you're losing, ice block. Don't bother building for Armor or Lifesteal until Round 3.

Alright! Now that you have 100 "free" Armor from [Frost Armor](item_f9925f6e-bb6a-4de6-bb86-622583d60779) on top of Mei's high baseline Health, the Life regeneration from [Martian Mender](item_0099632b-4e18-450e-844f-22c40e51bc98) will be especially potent. At first, it'll take ~18 seconds of primary fire uptime to fully stack your Armor, and then you'll be permanently regenerating ~13 Life per second. Both of these numbers will improve as your stats increase each round.

The passive regeneration is *not* going to make you incredibly tanky on its own. The reason why it's so good is because it's *always* ticking. Every precious moment that you spend at less than 100% Life, you're getting value from it. That gives it an extreme advantage over Lifesteal when it comes to self-sufficiency.

That said, this build *does* also feature active healing via [Phantasmic Flux](item_5e644a79-cf6e-4196-8d0a-232f75004643). You'll be gaining more Weapon Power soon, but even just at a baseline, this item will heal you for ~17 Life per second as long as you're spraying an enemy with your primary fire. Even better, if you've already been Martian Mended up to full, shooting enemies will grant you an extra buffer of up to 100 Overhealth.

For frame of reference, Mercy's healing beam restores 60 Life per second. So between the passive regeneration and the Lifesteal, that means playing this build is like being pocketed by half a Mercy! And though it's not integral to the game plan, getting 10% Cooldown Reduction and 10% Ability Power is a neat little bonus.

Synergizing beautifully with everything else, [Weapon Jammer](item_72386db6-753e-413d-aa2a-f1389842f47f) pumps another 25 Armor into your Life pool while granting you a cost-efficient 10% Weapon Power *and* 10% Attack Speed. [Iceberg](item_312193a7-1f88-462f-93fe-9a60f4462d47) is a pretty good general utility power. When you're walling enemies off, you're usually doing it to isolate them and kill them before they can flee. Turning the wall into a more dangerous obstacle helps to accomplish that goal.

When it comes to securing eliminations, there's no better item than [Eye of the Spider](item_bbaf01d7-340d-4199-b738-86a98d68fe9b). +25% Weapon Power is a big deal overall, and the additional x1.1 multiplier against near-death enemies is the *icing* on the cake.

The 15% stagger from [Nebula Conduit](item_476b7040-54c9-4f0c-8283-b4407f6809f8) is terrific. At the start of a fight, it keeps you within your Armor margin for 15% longer. At the end of a fight, your constant Life regeneration negates the downside of the delayed damage. +50 Health and +5% Weapon Power aren't as special, but both of those raw stats contribute to this build's self-healing.

If you've made it all the way to Round 7, your enemies are gonna be dealing some *crazy* damage. This is the time to take all the additive Life bonuses you've gained, and culminate them into maximum-value multiplicative defensive picks.

Your final power, [Blizznado](item_208ab663-2529-489a-87d9-d798d94f4c22), grants you supercharged Life regeneration during your ultimate. When you drop a blizzard on the objective, you *will* hold that objective, at least for several seconds. Thanks to [Iceberg](item_312193a7-1f88-462f-93fe-9a60f4462d47), you can also combo this effect with your ice wall in a pinch.

[Rustung Von Wilhelm](item_aea17a63-3f55-4f91-8f49-a7793fbc56c4) is only worth taking if you already have a massive Life pool... and at this final hour the match, you certainly do. The main draw is how much additional regeneration it contributes to your [Martian Mender](item_0099632b-4e18-450e-844f-22c40e51bc98), but the 10% damage reduction under 30% Life can come in clutch. Though you won't be lingering on the brink of death very often, it just might give you the split-second you need to recharge your ice block or ice wall cooldown.
